# Alert dialog

A dialog that interrupts to confirm an action that cannot be undone.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Multi-brand</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-alert-dialog--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:multi-brand--aster;mode:light" title="Alert dialog examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-alert-dialog--docs">Open Alert dialog in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-alert-dialog--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:multi-brand--aster;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Multi-brand:** Cancel a plan.

- **Use it when:** Deleting, cancelling or overwriting something people cannot get back, when undo is not possible.
- **Not when:** Anything that can be undone (offer undo instead), or a form or task (use a dialog).

Instead:

- [Dialog](./dialog.md): A focused task, not a confirmation.
- [Toast](./toast.md): Undo after the fact, when the action can be reversed.

## How Multi-brand uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Delete or remove</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Button secondary, then confirm with Button danger</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Button primary</div></div><div class="cap">Confirm before destroying data.</div></div><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">A confirmation question</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> Shared across brands: plain and specific</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> Brand tone when something is lost</div></div><div class="cap">Loss is never the moment for personality. Example: “Cancel your plan? It stays active until the end of the month.”</div></div></div>

## Words

- Shared structure: object, state, next step.
- Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
- Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
- Use: Get started, Plan, Order. Avoid: Brand-specific words in errors, Jargon.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Get started

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Escape cancels, the same as the safe choice. | undefined |
| undefined | Tab stays inside until people choose. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is an alertdialog with a title and a description that names the consequence. undefined
- [ ] Focus starts on the safe choice, never on the destructive one. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add alert-dialog
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Variables

Every token Alert dialog reads, from its code: the variable, the semantic token it aliases, and where that ends in the theme.
